text.p: Juventus face their first major test of the Italian league season at home to Fiorentina on Sunday.
The European Cup holders have moved joint top of serie A by collecting seven points against lowly Reggiana, Cagliari and Perugia in their opening three games.
Fiorentina, pre-season Italian Super Cup winners against AC Milan, are an entirely different proposition as Juventus coach Marcello Lippi readily acknowledges.
"Fiorentina beat Milan, beat them well and on merit in a real game and they remain one of seven sides you have to fancy for the league title," he said.
Juventus will be without suspended French midfielder Zinedine Zidane, due to be replaced by Serb Vladimir Jugovic. Defender Moreno Torricelli returns from injury in place of Sergio Porrini.
Up front, the Turin side again rely on in-form Croat Alen Boksic partnered by Alessandro Del Piero and Christian Vieri.
Fiorentina defeated Gloria Bistrita of Romania in the European Cup Winners' Cup on Thursday but the 1-0 second leg result failed to impress coach Claudio Ranieri or the fans.
"If we play like that against Juventus, you'll want an abacus to keep the score," he said.
"There was no positive aspect to this performance, we simply didn't play."

Fiorentina have a full strength squad available, with Argentine captain Gabriel Batistuta leading the attack along with Brazilian Oliveira. Swede Stefan Schwarz partners Portugal's Rui Costa in midfield.
Ranieri's biggest selection problem concerns the choice between Massimo Orlando, scorer against Bistrita, Anselmo Robbiati and Sandro Cois in midfield.
Milan appear to have a straightforward task at home to newly-promoted Perugia, having renewed their confidence by thrashing Rosenborg in the European Cup Champions' League on Wednesday.

Marco Simone, scorer of nine goals in eight league and cup games this season including a hat-trick against the Norwegians, keeps out Roberto Baggio. He will again be partnered in attack by Liberian George Weah.
Injured Montenegrin Dejan Savicevic will be replaced by Stefan Eranio alongside Massimo Ambrosini, Croat Zvonimir Boban and Demetrio Albertini in a four-man midfield.
Captain Franco Baresi remains out injured and will be replaced in defence by Frenchman Marcel Desailly.
Perugia, unlucky in a 2-1 home loss to Juventus last week, may replace Croat striker Milan Rapjaic with experienced midfielder Fausto Pizzi.
Parma, the only loser among seven Italian sides in European competition this week, face a difficult visit to Lazio.
Coach Carlo Ancelotti said: "The league title remains our only target and I'd better be clear, we're not obliged to win it but we'd better give it a good try."
Lazio may again drop last season's leading scorer Igor Protti, preferring an attack of Giuseppe Signori, Pierluigi Casiraghi and Roberto Rambaudi.

Fixtures (all games Sunday): Atalanta v Internazionale, Lazio v Parma, AC Milan v Perugia, Piacenza v Vicenza, Reggiana v AS Roma, Sampdoria v Napoli, Udinese v Bologna, Vicenza v Cagliari, Juventus v Fiorentina.
